clue.text: Little half of capital from old city

parts.note: a baby is a little one, so little gives baby

indicators.note: half of the capital's name means its first three of six letters are kept

parts.note: the capital here is London, the UK capital

explanation.surface: A small piece of a capital city traced back to an ancient one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the first three of the capital's six letters; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the great ancient city of Mesopotamia on the Euphrates.

clue.text: French animal left nut

parts.note: bête is the French word for an animal or beast

explanation.surface: A French creature has abandoned a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is the areca nut chewed with betel leaves across South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Caber is tossed in Italy

indicators.note: tossing jumbles things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Highland games caber is being tossed somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges CABER and IS; 'in Italy' defines a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city of Lombardy in northern Italy, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Preferably … speak truth piano?

parts.note: the question mark asks for the opposite: the contrary of speaking truth is to tell an untruth
piano means soft in music; its opposite, forte or loud, is abbreviated F

explanation.surface: Would one rather tell the truth softly?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flips both pieces: the opposite of 'speak truth' is LIE, and the opposite of 'piano' (soft) is forte, F. So LIE F is 'speak truth piano' turned inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lief is an old adverb meaning gladly or willingly, as in I would as lief stay, so it means preferably.

clue.text: Far from how an 8 13 may be reached? Far from it

definitions.text: Far from how an 8 13 may be reached?
definitions.meaning: 8 and 13 are a distant blackboard: you could only reach a far-off board with an extended stick of chalk, and 'far from' that is the negation
an idiom meaning not at all, by no means

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: a distant blackboard is reached 'by a long chalk', and 'Far from' puts NOT in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means not at all or by no means, the same as far from it.

clue.text: Little flower transformed our little debutantes

indicators.note: transforming changes shape, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: debs is the short form of debutantes, young women coming out in society

explanation.surface: Our young society girls have blossomed into something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges OUR plus DEBS (debutantes shortened, hence 'little').
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is the unopened bud of a rose, a flower not yet grown.

clue.text: My old man (suitably clad) said: "Don't put money in the tin"

definitions.meaning: the music-hall song My Old Man's a Dustman; suitably dressed, he is a binman

definitions.text: Don't put money in the tin
definitions.meaning: read as an instruction: turn down the person shaking the collecting tin

explanation.walkthrough: The song 'My Old Man's a Dustman' gives the first sense; a dustman is a British binman. The second splits the phrase as refuse (decline) plus collector, the charity tin-rattler.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman, the subject of the old song, is formally called by this job title, as a council employee clearing bins.

clue.text: Shed tears for saint in account of lottery

indicators.note: in places the tears and saint inside the word for account

parts.note: sake means account, as in for my sake or on my account
to weep is to shed tears

explanation.surface: Someone cries over a saint in the story of a lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the tears and the saint inside the word for account, splitting it after its first letter; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery-style draw in which the stakes are pooled and paid to the winners.

clue.text: See 9
Far from the underworld with so much French

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
tant is French for so much

explanation.surface: Far from Hades with a great deal of French.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant and far are synonyms for something a long way off.

clue.text: Pessimistic message from old city to fast-breeder reactor: it is "Hard cheese!"

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city of Egypt, and also of Greece
taken as written
FBR is the abbreviation for a fast-breeder reactor
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
in the idiom hard cheese, cheese stands for fortune, so it gives the word for chance

explanation.surface: An ancient city sends a nuclear plant a curt note of commiseration.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in clue order. 'Hard cheese' is British slang for bad fortune, so 'cheese' stands for the luck in it. The phrase is said ironically, expecting failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishing someone this is usually ironic, implying they will need fortune because they are likely to fail.

clue.text: Prophet of Israel, I assume

indicators.note: of says the answer is made of letters from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A prophet of Israel, I take it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through isra-EL I AS-sume. Reading 'Prophet of Israel' together is the trap: the definition is just 'Prophet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet, used in the New Testament.

clue.text: See 9
It has little flowers happily arranged on a string like this inside

parts.note: G is one of the strings of a violin

indicators.note: inside places the words for like this within the jumbled letters
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: Something bears tiny blooms, prettily threaded on a string like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' scrambles the letters of happily, 'inside' puts the word for like this within them, and the violin string goes 'on' at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsophila, baby's breath, is a plant bearing clouds of tiny white flowers.

clue.text: Illustrator and poet are without box office input

indicators.note: input means put in, so the following pieces go inside the poet

parts.note: a bard is a poet
to lack something is to be without it

explanation.surface: An artist and a poet have no say in ticket sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illustrator and poet' tempts as Blake, who was both; but 'Illustrator' alone is the definition, and 'input' puts the other two pieces inside the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher illustrates lessons on it, so a chalked board is fairly called an illustrator.

clue.text: Composer left a little bit of nonsense

parts.note: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer

explanation.surface: A composer has left behind a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fal-lal is a frivolous trinket or piece of finery, a trifling bit of foolishness.

clue.text: Be punished with punishment note

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, was a whip used for punishment
a chit is a short note or voucher

explanation.surface: Accept punishment along with a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in trouble and receive a scolding or penalty is an idiomatic way to say be punished.

clue.text: Arrive with old arrangement for mutual assistance

parts.note: to come is to arrive
con is Italian (and musical) for with

explanation.surface: Turn up bearing an outdated mutual aid pact.
explanation.definitionFit: Comecon was the Soviet bloc's Council for Mutual Economic Assistance, dissolved in 1991.

clue.text: Financial resources of those said to have a tickle in the throat?

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.words: to have a tickle in the throat
parts.note: people with a tickle in the throat are coughers

explanation.surface: Money matters of people who can't stop clearing their throats?
explanation.walkthrough: 'those ... to have a tickle in the throat' are COUGHERS, and 'said' makes it sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes, and by extension the funds or treasury of an organisation.

clue.text: Tennis player's time in boat yard

indicators.note: in puts the time letter inside the boat yard

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for boats and yachts

explanation.surface: A tennis player is spending time in a boat yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Martina Navratilova and Martina Hingis are famous tennis players with this name.

clue.text: Odds on looking good?

definitions.meaning: odds-on means probable, expected to happen

explanation.surface: A racegoer's verdict on a promising horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Likely means probable, and also promising or suitable, as in a likely candidate.

clue.text: 8 in time to see number (including silencer)

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see

indicators.note: including says the number holds the silencer

parts.note: a gag silences someone

explanation.surface: Far back in time, to look at a number with a silencer on.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is DISTANT, so '8 in time' means distant in time; 'including' puts the silencer inside the number, and 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distant in time happened in the remote past.

clue.text: Rebus nearly found in cockney's dense shrubbery with extinguisher

indicators.note: found in places the shortened word inside the shrubbery

parts.note: a thicket is dense shrubbery; a cockney says th as f

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture puzzle turns up in a Londoner's thicket alongside fire-fighting gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, say TH as F, so the thicket loses its TH sound; 'nearly' cuts the last letter of rebus, and 'found in' puts the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket of water or sand hung up for fires is a basic extinguisher.

clue.text: Detective man, turning pale, to work with teeth

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI detective, giving G

indicators.note: turning means the word for pale is read backwards

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: An investigator going white starts gnashing at something.
explanation.walkthrough: From G-MAN, the 'man' turns into a backwards WAN: G plus NAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnaw is to bite or chew at something persistently with the teeth.

clue.text: Dilute 26's forerunner when the boat comes in

indicators.note: the boat coming in would complete the novel's title, so the answer is that title without it

parts.note: Richard Adams wrote his famous rabbit novel before Shardik, the answer at 26
a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: Thin something out as the vessel docks after the earlier novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put SHIP into the answer and you get Adams's earlier title, so the answer is that title less SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a drink is to thin it with liquid, the sense of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: See 22
Heather is wealthy in Rome

definitions.meaning: a genus name for heaths and heathers
Italian è ricca, she is rich, sounds like this word

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is Italian: è ricca means she is wealthy, said much like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths, so it names heather.

clue.text: Traveller going for tour with Satan

indicators.note: going here means gone to pieces, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A traveller swaps a tour for a trip with the Devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' rearranges TOUR and SATAN; 'for' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a traveller in space.

clue.text: Princess swallowed by fish or bear

indicators.note: swallowed by puts the princess inside the fish

parts.note: a shark is a fish
Di, short for Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A princess is eaten by a fish, or perhaps by a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shardik is the giant bear in Richard Adams's 1974 novel of that name.

clue.text: No officer is reported for ill-feeling

indicators.note: is reported signals a word heard, not read

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, not a commissioned officer

explanation.surface: An enlisted man is reported for bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, RANKER sounds much like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment or ill will.
